description: ICS Village at DEF CON 33 focuses on industrial control systems, operational technology, SCADA networks, and critical infrastructure protection. Talks cover OT SOC workflows, protocol gateway discovery, DMZ breaching techniques, and Common Industrial Protocol exploitation.

talks.title: The Worst ICS/OT Love Story Ever Told
talks.teaser: Analyzes how the rapid proliferation of advanced tools among low-skilled attackers is reshaping threats against operational technology networks.
talks.summary:
Rapid Evolution of Industrial Cyber Threats

Operational Technology (OT) and Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are experiencing rapid shifts in adversary capabilities and attack frequency. Industrial environments previously shielded by obscurity now face persistent, targeted scanning and exploitation.

Transition from State Actors to Opportunistic Groups

While state-sponsored Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) historically dominated ICS security discourse, current threat telemetry demonstrates that ransomware gangs and hacktivists are actively probing industrial networks for vulnerable edge appliances and exposed control interfaces.

Accessibility of Advanced Attack Tooling

Exploitation frameworks, automated scanners, and default protocol interaction tools are increasingly accessible to low-skilled threat actors. This commoditization enables attackers with minimal industrial expertise to trigger significant operational disruptions.

Strategic Roadmaps for OT Resilience

Defending industrial networks requires establishing active asset inventory, implementing robust network zoning between enterprise IT and operational zones, and training operational staff on cyber-incident recognition.

talks.title: Don’t Cry Wolf: Evidence Based Assessments of ICS Threats
talks.teaser: Shares practical threat hunting queries and analysis methodologies used by Dragos to differentiate genuine ICS malware from benign research or IT threats on VirusTotal.
talks.summary:
Hunting for Novel ICS Malware in Public Repositories

While bespoke Industrial Control Systems (ICS) malware remains rare, landmark threats such as TRISIS, FrostyGoop, and COSMICENERGY were initially discovered in public repositories like VirusTotal.

Filtering Benign Artifacts from Malicious ICS Code

Threat hunters regularly encounter benign research tools, CTF artifacts, and obfuscated junk code that trigger superficial ICS detection keywords. Establishing rigorous triage queries prevents false alarms and wasted investigative cycles.

Analytical Workflow and Victim Notification

Dragos analysts walk through systematic hunting queries, static binary analysis workflows, and validation protocols used to confirm whether a suspicious binary possesses true operational technology disruption capabilities.

Applying Dragos ICS Malware Classification

Applying a formal, evidence-based ICS malware taxonomy ensures accurate threat reporting, responsible industry alerts, and swift victim notifications when actionable critical infrastructure threats emerge.

talks.title: Locked Down, Not Locked Out: How I Escaped Yr Secure Operator Workstation
talks.teaser: Details breakout and privilege escalation tradecraft against hardened industrial operator workstations using living-off-the-land techniques.
talks.summary:
The False Sense of Workstation Hardening

Critical infrastructure facilities and manufacturing plants rely on locked-down operator workstations to safeguard operational control systems. However, restrictive shell configurations often fail to prevent local breakout and privilege escalation.

Common Breakout Vectors in Industrial Kiosks

Penetration tester Aaron Boyd demonstrates how standard operator accounts exploit misconfigured file dialogues, help menus, shortcut keys, and administrative helper utilities to spawn interactive command prompts.

Living Off the Land in Constrained Environments

Once a shell is established, operators leverage native Windows executables, PowerShell scripts, and diagnostic tools already present on the endpoint to enumerate local permissions, bypass application whitelisting, and escalate to SYSTEM privileges.

Practical Hardening and Monitoring Controls

Securing industrial workstations requires enforcing AppLocker and Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) in block mode, disabling unnecessary OS shortcut hooks, and monitoring for anomalous process spawning from operator interfaces.

talks.title: Safeguarding the Industrial Frontier: OT SOC & Incident Response
talks.teaser: Explores specialized incident response strategies and operational considerations required to build and run effective Security Operations Centers in OT environments.
talks.summary:
Bridging IT and OT Security Operations

As industrial enterprises connect operational technology (OT) to enterprise IT networks, building dedicated OT Security Operations Center (SOC) capabilities has become essential to safeguard physical processes from cyber threats.

Unique Operational Constraints in Industrial SOCs

Unlike traditional IT SOCs that focus on data confidentiality and endpoint isolation, OT SOCs prioritize system availability, process safety, and physical uptime. Standard IT containment actions—such as shutting down hosts or blocking subnets—can cause catastrophic physical shutdowns.

Specialized OT Incident Response Playbooks

Adam Robbie details how organizations must develop incident response playbooks tailored to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), distributed control systems (DCS), and proprietary industrial protocols.

Continuous Monitoring and Threat Telemetry

Effective OT defense relies on passive network monitoring, protocol anomaly detection, and close collaboration between cybersecurity analysts and frontline plant control engineers.

talks.title: Deploying Deception in Depth for ICS
talks.teaser: Presents strategies for designing and deploying cyber deception across industrial control systems using the MITRE Engage framework, focused on APT44 TTPs.
talks.summary:
Cyber Deception in Critical Infrastructure

Deploying defensive deception within Industrial Control Systems (ICS) provides high-fidelity early warning alerts and alters adversary economics by injecting decoys into operational networks.

Operationalizing the MITRE Engage Framework

Brent Muir outlines how industrial defenders can adapt the MITRE Engage framework to map deception activities directly to adversary goals, establishing intentional decoys across OT DMZs and control zones.

Case Study: Defending Against APT44 TTPs

Focusing on threat actor APT44 (Sandworm), the presentation illustrates how emulated programmable logic controllers (PLCs), synthetic industrial protocol responders, and deceptive engineering workstations trap sophisticated attackers.

Engineering Considerations and Safety Guardrails

Designing OT deception requires strict safety controls to prevent honeypot systems from interfering with real-time industrial processes or creating operational hazards.

talks.title: There and Back Again: Detecting OT Devices Across Protocol Gateways
talks.teaser: Details network discovery tradecraft for enumerating OT assets behind protocol translation gateways using CIP message forwarding and DNP3 discovery.
talks.summary:
The Reality of OT/IT Network Convergence

Industrial Control Systems (ICS) increasingly adopt commodity TCP/IP networking, connecting proprietary field devices to enterprise networks through protocol translation gateways.

Visibility Challenges Behind Protocol Gateways

Protocol gateways translate standard TCP/IP traffic into proprietary serial or fieldbus communications. Standard IT network scanners cannot enumerate devices residing behind these gateway boundaries, creating major asset visibility blind spots.

CIP Message Forwarding and DNP3 Discovery

Rob King details practical techniques for querying devices through gateways, demonstrating how Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) routing and DNP3 address discovery mechanisms can be leveraged to enumerate hidden field assets.

Actionable Reconnaissance for Industrial Defenders

Implementing protocol-aware discovery techniques enables defenders to build accurate asset inventories, identify legacy endpoints, and enforce proper network segmentation across industrial facilities.

talks.title: Crossing the Line: Advanced Techniques to Breach the OT DMZ
talks.teaser: Explores offensive tradecraft for bypassing DMZ segmentation and pivoting from enterprise footholds into industrial control networks.
talks.summary:
The OT DMZ as a Critical Security Boundary

The demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating enterprise IT networks from operational technology (OT) control zones is designed to enforce strict isolation. However, operational conveniences often introduce severe segmentation weaknesses.

Pivoting from Enterprise Footholds

Christopher Nourrie demonstrates how red team operators leverage initial IT access to identify and abuse misconfigured remote access solutions, jump hosts, Citrix gateways, and RDP relays spanning the IT/OT boundary.

Lateral Movement and Credential Abuse in the DMZ

Techniques for proxying traffic, abusing dual-homed systems, and extracting cached administrative credentials within the DMZ allow attackers to bypass intended Purdue Model network boundaries.

Hardening Industrial Perimeter Defenses

Defending the OT perimeter requires eliminating dual-homed jump hosts, enforcing dedicated multi-factor authentication on industrial access portals, and monitoring east-west network traffic across the DMZ.

talks.title: Let AI Autogenerate Neural ASR Rules for OT Attacks via NLP
talks.teaser: Introduces Suspicious2Vec, an NLP-based multimodal AI model that establishes baseline industrial operations to generate neural attack surface reduction rules.
talks.summary:
Living-Off-the-Land Attacks in Industrial Networks

Sophisticated threat actors targeting industrial control systems (such as Sandworm in Ukraine) routinely abuse benign OT-specific protocols, LOLBins, and native engineering utilities to evade conventional EDR detection.

Suspicious2Vec: Multimodal AI for Industrial Baselines

Mars Cheng and Jr Wei-Huang present Suspicious2Vec, an NLP-inspired multimodal AI framework that learns contextual baselines of normal factory operations by converting industrial system behaviors into numerical vector embeddings.

Autogenerating Neural Attack Surface Reduction Rules

Trained on a massive dataset of 2,000,000 operational events and malware profiles from VirusTotal, the model autogenerates neural Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules that accurately differentiate benign operational anomalies from malicious Living-Off-the-Land techniques.

Validation on Factory Environments

Deploying Suspicious2Vec across operational manufacturing plants successfully detected 12 novel variant OT malware strains across more than 52,000 program files with minimal false positives.

talks.title: Intro to Common Industrial Protocol Exploitation
talks.teaser: Introduces the fundamentals of the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) used in factory automation and demonstrates techniques for industrial protocol testing.

talks.title: Critically Neglected: Cybersecurity for buildings
talks.teaser: Explores systemic cybersecurity vulnerabilities in building management systems, HVAC controls, and physical facility automation networks.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Landscape of Building Automation

Modern commercial facilities rely on Building Management Systems (BMS) to control HVAC systems, power distribution, fire suppression, and physical access. These automation systems are frequently deployed with minimal cybersecurity oversight.

Insecure Protocols in Facility Automation

Protocols like BACnet, Modbus, and LonWorks were designed decades ago without authentication or encryption. When building automation networks are connected to corporate IT or exposed to the internet, attackers can manipulate physical environmental controls.

Case Studies of Building Compromises

Thomas Pope reviews real-world security assessments where compromised HVAC controllers allowed attackers to pivot into corporate subnets, manipulate datacenter cooling, or trigger physical facility lockouts.

Hardening Facility Control Systems

Securing building automation requires isolating BMS networks from corporate IT, deploying protocol-aware firewalls, disabling unneeded remote management portals, and establishing strict vendor maintenance access controls.
